title: Work as Area Under a Force Graph
short: The area under a force–position graph is the work done.
trouble: Students multiply the final force by the distance when the force changes along the way.

blocks.html: $W = Fd$ needs one steady force. A spring's force grows as you stretch it, and a rocket's thrust changes as it climbs. A graph of force against position handles any of them, the same way the area under a v–t graph gave displacement.
The work done by a force along a straight path is the area under its force-position ($F$–$x$) graph, counted negative where the force is negative.

Slice the path into short steps. Over each step the force is nearly constant, so the work there is $F\,\Delta x$: the area of a thin strip. Adding up all the strips adds up the work. For a force that changes, using the final force times the whole distance counts the big end value over the whole path and overestimates the work.

blocks.name: ph-graph

opts.task: Drag the right edge. The shaded triangle is the work needed to stretch the spring that far.

blocks.cap: Stretching a spring with k = 200 N/m by 0.3 m: the area is ½ × 0.3 × 60 = 9 J, not 60 × 0.3 = 18 J.

blocks.title: A spring
blocks.q: Stretching a spring from $0$ to $0.3\ \text{m}$, the force rises steadily from $0$ to $60\ \text{N}$. How much work do you do?
steps: The area under the straight line is a triangle.

blocks.title: A changing push
blocks.q: A cart is pushed with $10\ \text{N}$ for the first $2\ \text{m}$; then the push falls steadily to $0$ over the next $4\ \text{m}$. Find the total work.

blocks.title: A force that reverses
blocks.q: A force is $+8\ \text{N}$ from $x = 0$ to $3\ \text{m}$, then $-4\ \text{N}$ from $3$ to $5\ \text{m}$. Find the net work.

blocks.html: Multiplying the final force by the distance when the force changes along the way. For the spring above that gives $18\ \text{J}$, twice the right answer. Check: sketch the $F$–$x$ graph and find the area; $F_{final} \times d$ is the area of the rectangle around it, too big whenever the force grew.
